prompt_text: I need my roof replaced in Dallas. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
engine_stated_criteria: Do not hire a roofer who offers to waive or “cover” your insurance deductible
answer_verbatim:
For a Dallas roof replacement, I’d call these **three first**, then add a fourth if the scopes or prices are far apart:

1. **Kidd Roofing** — Best all-around first call  
   - Long-established Dallas–Fort Worth roofing company with both residential and commercial experience.  
   - A good fit for a larger, more complex roof, steep-slope roof, extensive flashing/decking concerns, or if you want a contractor with a mature estimating and warranty process.  
   - Ask them to quote the exact shingle system, ventilation changes, flashing, decking allowance, gutters, and workmanship warranty separately.

2. **Lon Smith Roofing** — Good benchmark from a long-tenured North Texas roofer  
   - A very established DFW company with the scale to handle replacement work and post-install service.  
   - Worth including because their bid can serve as a useful “established-company” comparison against smaller firms.  
   - Especially useful if you want a company that can also discuss repair-vs-replace honestly, rather than treating every roof as an automatic full replacement.

3. **CLC Roofing** — Strong local residential-roofing comparison  
   - A longtime DFW-area roofing specialist and a good counterbalance to the larger firms above.  
   - Call them if you want a more hands-on local-company option while still seeking a formal written scope and warranty.  
   - Ask for recent completed jobs in your neighborhood or similar homes—not just online reviews.

4. **Phillips Home Improvements** — Best if the project may include gutters, fascia, siding, paint, or other exterior work  
   - More of a broader exterior/home-improvement contractor than a roof-only choice.  
   - Useful if your roof replacement will uncover related work, such as damaged fascia, chimney trim, gutters, or exterior painting.  
   - For a straightforward roofing-only job, still compare their proposal against Kidd, Lon Smith, and CLC.

## My practical recommendation

Call **Kidd Roofing, Lon Smith Roofing, and CLC Roofing** for the initial three bids. Add **Phillips Home Improvements** if you expect exterior work beyond the roof.

That gives you:
- one established, roofing-focused larger firm;
- one very long-running DFW benchmark;
- one local residential specialist;
- and, if needed, one broader exterior contractor.

## What to require from every bid

Do not compare only the bottom-line number. Give each company the same requested scope and ask for it in writing:

- Full tear-off or overlay? For a replacement, full tear-off is usually preferable.
- Number of existing layers to remove.
- Exact shingle manufacturer, product line, color, and impact-resistance rating.
- Whether they will replace all pipe boots, valley metal, flashing, drip edge, and damaged vents.
- Price per sheet for any rotten decking found after tear-off.
- Ventilation plan: intake and exhaust, not merely “add vents.”
- Underlayment type and where leak barrier will be installed.
- Gutters, chimney flashing, skylights, solar-panel removal/reinstall, and cleanup.
- Start/completion timing and who will be your on-site project manager.
- Written workmanship-warranty length and what is excluded.
- Proof of general liability and workers’ compensation coverage.
- Three recent local references for roofs installed at least a year ago.

## Dallas-specific cautions

- **Do not hire a roofer who offers to waive or “cover” your insurance deductible.** That is a major red flag and can create legal/insurance problems in Texas.
- Texas does not have a broad statewide roofing-contractor license, so insurance, local reputation, manufacturer credentials, references, and a detailed contract matter more than a generic “licensed and insured” claim.
- Manufacturer certifications can be helpful, but verify them directly on the manufacturer’s website; they change over time and are not a substitute for good installation.
- If this is an insurance claim, choose the contractor based on their written scope and workmanship—not on who promises the biggest claim payment.

If you share your Dallas ZIP code, roof type/material, approximate size, and whether this is storm/insurance-related, I can narrow this to the best two or three calls and give you a bid-comparison checklist tailored to your roof.
